# OpenLineage operations workspace

A private, editable operations workspace for original OpenLineage events.
Receive a producer's HTTP events or import original JSON, NDJSON or gzip files,
inspect their jobs, runs and datasets, follow
the reported dependencies, save an edition, record an operator decision and
attach a complete result to the event context that explains it. Deliver that
whole workspace, including the original files and editable application, to
another operator.

The browser, command line, Node SDK and MCP tools use the same revisioned
workspace. The maintained SCF distribution adds this product to its existing
command catalog and Applications lifecycle. Its source-owned merchant provider adds
22 tools over this same original application; see [MERCHANT.md](MERCHANT.md).

## Start

Node 22 or newer is the only runtime dependency. A received application can
run directly from its own directory; there is no package installation step.

    node cli.mjs init --workspace /absolute/private/lineage --title "Data operations"
    node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/private/lineage --port 8767

Open the printed local URL. The browser has source import, a searchable
jobs/runs/datasets inventory, original event and facet inspection, lineage,
saved editions and comparison, reasoned reviews, attached result files and
complete downloads. Existing projects reopen through the same command.

In the maintained installed distribution:

    starforge openlineage init --workspace /absolute/private/lineage
    starforge openlineage serve --workspace /absolute/private/lineage
    starforge registrations --source openlineage-workspace

Applications lists **OpenLineage operations**. Select the initialized or
received workspace and an optional private token file, then use the existing
Review, Save, Review Start, Start, Open and Stop controls. The adapter binds the
original workspace identity and selected source to that existing lifecycle.

## Import original events

Select a complete source file in the browser or use:

    node cli.mjs import --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
      --input /absolute/producer/events.ndjson \
      --source https://your-producer.example/retained-job-log \
      --operation-id producer-capture-20261012

The CLI infers the current revision unless --revision is supplied. Reuse the
same operation ID and exact original arguments after an interrupted response.
A new intended source import gets its own ID.

Import accepts one JSON event, an array of JSON events, or NDJSON. Every
original source byte is retained under its SHA-256. Logical events deduplicate
by canonical complete event content; later observations with changed facets
remain distinct even when their run and event type match. The source inspector
retains the original source position and diagnostic for each event.

The source URL is an operator-supplied provenance field. The application does
not fetch it. Source downloads return the exact retained bytes.

### Producer HTTP transport

Native Python, Java, Airflow and other OpenLineage HTTP clients can send their
original bodies to:

    POST http://127.0.0.1:8767/api/v1/lineage

The receiver accepts uncompressed or gzip JSON/NDJSON. It retains compressed
wire bytes unchanged and verifies their decoded byte identity. Native producer
arrivals use the original workspace writer through a serial append queue.
A response acknowledges the source only after its original operation is saved.

The optional Idempotency-Key header selects the original operation ID. By
default it is derived from the unchanged wire body. Repeat the exact body,
name, reference and encoding after a lost response. An explicitly supplied
If-Match retains its numeric revision check. Queue or writer backpressure
returns 503 with Retry-After: 1.

Use the browser's **Producer intake** control to inspect the actual endpoint,
current queue and server counters and download complete Python or Java client
settings. The CLI's producer-config command creates the same private
configuration from the actual connection.json. A separate producer token can
admit events while the operator token controls the whole workspace.

[PRODUCERS.md](PRODUCERS.md) covers complete client setup, authentication, gzip,
source inspection, retries, capacity and the native producer receiving journey.

The explicit operator import route, /api/sources?name=events.ndjson&source=URL,
keeps its normal revision checks. It also accepts Content-Encoding: gzip.
To import a compressed original directly through the CLI, add
--content-encoding gzip to the import command and retain the .gz filename.

## Operate the project

1. Import complete producer files. Inspect any source diagnostics before
   choosing the event set to review.
2. Open a job, dataset or run. Namespaces are part of identity. Runs retain their
   native UUID plus the owning job identity. Inspect original facets and input
   and output observations alongside the graph.
3. Save a named edition. It retains the current event IDs and source IDs; later
   imports do not change that saved selection.
4. Compare two editions, or a saved edition with the live project. Inspect
   added events and changed jobs, datasets and run outcomes.
5. Save a review against selected entities. A reason is required. Decisions are
   accepted, needs-work, excluded or observed. Updating a review retains its
   previous text, selection and decision in the review's history.
6. Attach the complete existing result file to its saved edition and entities.
   Keep its source reference and, where applicable, its original query alongside
   the bytes. CSV, JSON, reports and other file formats remain their original
   files.
7. Export the complete workspace or generate its complete JSON, CSV or printable
   HTML report. Reopen the delivered workspace to continue the same history.

A review records a human or agent assessment. It does not erase an event,
rewrite the upstream pipeline outcome or cause an upstream job to run.
Result attachment carries existing bytes and their declared relationship to
the selected context.

## Deliver and receive

    node cli.mjs export --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
      --out /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json

The package contains the saved state, all source and attached-result objects,
and the complete portable application. Each object and application file has
its byte length and SHA-256; the complete payload has its own digest. Existing
workspace, event, edition, review and operation identities survive receiving.

    node cli.mjs verify --input /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json
    node cli.mjs receive --input /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json \
      --out /absolute/private/received-lineage
    node /absolute/private/received-lineage/application/cli.mjs serve \
      --workspace /absolute/private/received-lineage --port 8768

Receiving verifies the complete package before creating the destination. Use a
new destination directory. It restores exact original objects and reconstructs
event/source relationships from those original files, installs the included
application, and records a separate local installation ID in received.json.
Starting that received application is the explicit subsequent command.

Remote clients can download an existing export in exact, resumable byte ranges:

    node cli.mjs download --url http://127.0.0.1:8767 \
      --id EXPORT_SHA256 --out /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json

A partial download retains its original export identity and offset. Repeating
the command continues that export and verifies its complete digest before
making the destination file available.

## Node SDK

Import LineageClient from ./client.mjs or the installed
@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant package's /seller/openlineage export. The
adjacent client.d.ts declares the interface.

    import { LineageClient } from "./client.mjs";
    import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
    import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

    const client = new LineageClient("http://127.0.0.1:8767");
    const current = await client.read();
    const original = await readFile("/absolute/producer/events.ndjson");
    const imported = await client.importSource(original, {
      name: "events.ndjson",
      operationId: randomUUID(),
      expectedRevision: current.revision
    });
    const edition = await client.saveEdition({
      title: "Reviewed producer capture",
      operationId: randomUUID(),
      expectedRevision: imported.revision
    });

Keep the operation ID and exact arguments before sending a mutation if another
process will need to resume it. A 409 with the current revision means another
writer changed the project; read that change before issuing a new operation.
A replay with the same ID and original input returns the original result.

For a host-selected connection, the client supports expectedWorkspaceId and
instanceId. The server verifies these headers on the same request that performs
the action. The optional signal joins the caller's cancellation to the request
timeout.

The direct LineageWorkspace interface in store.mjs provides the same native
methods for a private local process.

## MCP and HTTP API

    node cli.mjs mcp --workspace /absolute/private/lineage

The stdio server uses newline-delimited JSON-RPC. It provides MCP initialize,
tools/list and tools/call for the native action catalog. The same stateless
JSON-RPC interface is available at POST /mcp. The declared protocol version is
2025-03-26.

POST /api/action accepts {"action":"workspace.read","args":{}} and returns the
native action result. Inspect catalog.mjs for exact input schemas. Mutation
arguments carry operationId and expectedRevision. Object and export downloads
have separate original-byte routes.

GET /api/identity returns the current original workspace and application
instance. The server writes that same small identity to the workspace's private
connection.json for an installed host adapter. GET /api/workspace returns the
current projection and saved history.

## Source interpretation

SOURCE_CONTRACT.md records the supported upstream schema versions, lifecycle,
facet replacement, graph rules and exact fixture provenance. Events outside the
supported operational grammar remain inspectable in their original source
with diagnostics. Native event timestamps order projections; source arrival
sequence resolves ties.

This workspace distinguishes declared job structure from individual run
observations. It follows explicit producer lineage when available and retains
the dataset-to-run-to-dataset graph when only input/output observations exist.
It does not manufacture an all-to-all dataset relationship from two event
arrays.

## Recovery and operation

The selected workspace directory holds workspace.json, content-addressed
objects/, immutable exports/, the current connection.json and a short-lived
writer.lock. Files created by the application use private permissions.

Only one mutation writes the saved state at a time. State updates use a
synchronized temporary file followed by an atomic rename. Stable operation IDs
make a lost success response recoverable. A process interruption may leave its
writer.lock. Read that original record and use:

    node cli.mjs recover-lock --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
      --id ORIGINAL_LOCK_ID

The recovery command checks that the exact original lock remains and that its
process no longer exists.

The default HTTP body limit is 64 MiB. The native producer queue has separate
wire and decoded capacity settings described in PRODUCERS.md. Direct source
imports have a 256 MiB wire/decoded ceiling, subject to available memory and disk. This first
implementation keeps the saved event index in memory for projection and writes
its JSON state atomically. Use a workspace per operational scope when the full
event history outgrows the available host.

The default listener is local to this computer. To bind another interface,
provide a private token file containing at least 24 characters. The server
rejects other browser origins, requires that token on its data routes and uses
the selected host consistently. Transport through a configured HTTPS service
is the operator's deployment responsibility.

## Original source and distribution

The source-owned contribution is in
distribution/contributions/openlineage-workspace.json; contribution.json here
retains its portable metadata. The command, typed client, native store/model,
MCP API, browser route manifest and Applications provider enter the existing
immutable-source builder. The managed provider uses the existing distribution's
lifecycle; the portable exported application runs independently.

browser-assets-loader.mjs is the unchanged original shared distribution
browser-assets.mjs, Git blob 63801fa838c0479e6ae156d9f155461f02df0cfb, retained
locally so the independently received application uses that same manifest
reader without an external package dependency.

# Original OpenLineage source contract

This application reads original OpenLineage events and retains their complete
source documents. Its operational projection has named, versioned adapters.
The original event and facet bytes remain the source of truth for further
producer-specific interpretation.

## Supported core versions

| Core version | Operational event kinds | Original schema |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1-0-1 | RunEvent | https://openlineage.io/spec/1-0-1/OpenLineage.json |
| 1-0-5 | RunEvent | https://openlineage.io/spec/1-0-5/OpenLineage.json |
| 2-0-2 | RunEvent, JobEvent, DatasetEvent | https://openlineage.io/spec/2-0-2/OpenLineage.json |

The adapter reads the original HTTPS schema origin, version and event-kind
fragment. The 1-0-1 RunEvent fragment uses /definitions/RunEvent; 1-0-5 uses
/$defs/RunEvent. The maintained upstream fluentd event_full.json declares
1-0-5 with the older /definitions/RunEvent fragment. The application retains
that exact declaration and names its compatibility interpretation
core-1-0-5-legacy-run-pointer in the original event record.

The adapters check the operational fields used for identity, chronology,
boundaries and facet projection: eventTime with a timezone, producer and
schemaURL URIs, namespaced job/dataset identities, native UUID run IDs,
declared lifecycle states, arrays of source datasets, and facet producer/schema
metadata. They retain other upstream and custom properties unchanged in each
parsed original event. A custom facet can be inspected without an installed
semantic graph adapter.

The operational adapter is explicit about the versions and fields it interprets.
Full arbitrary custom-facet JSON Schema evaluation belongs to the producer's
declared schema and is not performed by this dependency-free reader. Unsupported
or malformed operational events remain available with intake diagnostics and
their exact source file.

Official source:
https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/object-model/
https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/facets/

## Original identity and event order

A job or dataset is identified by its exact namespace and name. A run keeps
its native UUID together with the owning job namespace and name. Repeated UUIDs
under different jobs remain separate observations and produce a diagnostic.

Logical event identity is the SHA-256 of its complete canonical JSON value.
This permits a repeated original event in more than one source document while
preserving every source position. It does not collapse all events for a run,
or all events having the same lifecycle state.

Projection follows eventTime, including sub-millisecond fractional ordering,
then original intake sequence for ties. The workspace retains original
timestamps; it does not replace them with local receiving time.

Each source has a SHA-256 over its exact original wire bytes. Uncompressed
sources retain their original UTF-8 document. Gzip sources retain the compressed
request or file, contentEncoding, decodedBytes and decodedSha256. Their decoded
JSON/NDJSON goes through the same versioned parser. Array sources retain
zero-based member indexes; NDJSON sources retain one-based physical line
numbers. Blank NDJSON lines do not alter the remaining physical positions.
Original source downloads return the wire bytes. source.read with decode:true
also returns verified decoded bytes for a gzip original.

## Run lifecycle and metadata supplements

The current core makes eventType optional. When present, the adapter uses the
states declared by that version. START records the first start; COMPLETE,
FAIL and ABORT retain the original first terminal outcome and its timestamp.
A subsequent conflicting lifecycle observation stays in the event history
and adds a run issue. OTHER contributes metadata without resetting the outcome
or duration. A run lacking a lifecycle state remains OBSERVED.

JobType emissionPattern metadata is retained. COMPLETE_SNAPSHOT observations
replace the reported run boundary set; ordinary accumulative observations merge
new input/output identities. OTHER remains a metadata supplement. STREAMING or
SERVICE metadata does not imply that the absence of COMPLETE is a failed run.

Run-specific inputFacets and outputFacets stay with their original run
observations. They do not become global dataset facets.

## Facets and lineage

A later observation of a same-named facet replaces that facet's complete value.
The application does not recursively merge old nested facet fields into a new
producer declaration. A JobFacet or DatasetFacet with _deleted removes that
facet from the relevant current selection while the original event remains
inspectable.

JobEvent declarations remain a distinct job-level input/output structure.
RunEvent observations retain their own run boundaries. A later static job event
does not rewrite the inputs and outputs of an earlier run.

The explicit lineage adapter reads:

- LineageJobFacet entries from the original 1-0-0 LineageFacet schema.
- LineageDatasetFacet inputs and fields for the facet's owning dataset.
- Typed JOB and DATASET references, including a JOB's optional native runId.
- Field inputs, source field names, target field names, transformations, and
  complete original field metadata.
- The maintained ColumnLineageDatasetFacet family as a fallback when an
  explicit lineage declaration for that scope and target is absent.

A JOB reference without namespace/name uses the enclosing job as defined by
the facet. Empty explicit inputs remain an explicit absence of upstream
dependencies. Explicit facet replacement and deletion remove the superseded
relationships from the active graph. observedEdges retains the original
per-event relationship history.

When only event input/output arrays exist, the graph retains dataset-to-run
and run-to-dataset observations. It does not derive a dataset-to-dataset
Cartesian product. Where a run or job carries explicit lineage, its contextual
input/output boundaries remain separately available without allowing traversal
through those boundaries to invent extra dependencies. The lineage response
includes exact source event, facet path, schema and transformation context.

Official explicit facet:
https://openlineage.io/spec/facets/1-0-0/LineageFacet.json
https://openlineage.io/docs/spec/facets/job-facets/lineage/

## Saved editions, reviews and results

An edition captures the original source IDs and logical event IDs currently
present. Later intake leaves those identities unchanged. Edition comparison
reports added/removed/changed entity definitions and added original events.

Reviews record a decision and reason against original entity keys and,
optionally, a saved edition. Review revisions preserve the prior review record.
An attached result requires a real saved edition, existing entity selection,
complete file bytes and a source reference. Original result bytes are addressed
by SHA-256. The source reference and query explain the intended relationship;
the application does not infer a missing upstream execution from an attachment.

## Receiving

The receiver verifies the package payload and each complete object. It parses
every original source again to reconstruct event order, schema interpretation,
member positions and source references. Supplied indexes must agree with those
original bytes. Each edition's event membership must match its original selected
sources. Reviews and results must reference entities that exist in their selected
edition.

The export includes the entire portable application. Current packages declare
applicationVersion 2 and contain all 40 portable files, including the producer
queue, encoding adapter, typed producer configuration and complete operating
guides. Receiving still accepts the original 35-file application package without
applicationVersion. A gzip source requires the current application.

Receiving checks a compressed source's unchanged object hash, decoded length
and decoded hash before reconstructing its original event positions. It verifies
the complete declared application and installs it into application/; it preserves
workspace history and records a new local installation identity. Start the
application explicitly with its included CLI.

Hashes establish complete-byte identity and internal consistency. Source
origin is recorded through the supplied producer/source metadata and original
repository pins.

# OpenLineage in the merchant operator

The connected tools operate the same native HTTP workspace as the browser. Imports, event projections, saved editions, review history, results, and exports use the original workspace store and operation journal.

## Start the original workspace

Run the installed OpenLineage command, or the original source CLI:

~~~sh
node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/path/to/lineage-project --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

The startup JSON and the project's private connection.json contain its workspaceId, instanceId, and local origin. For a token-protected server, add --token-file with a private plain-text token file.

## Select workspace and complete file aliases

Save an owned private JSON file with mode 0600. Paths are relative to that file unless absolute. The workspaceId must come from the original project's startup record. SHA-256 values must cover every byte of each original input file.

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.openlineage-workspace-host.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "operations": {
      "label": "Production lineage",
      "connectionFile": "./lineage-project/connection.json",
      "workspaceId": "REPLACE_WITH_ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE_UUID",
      "timeoutMs": 120000,
      "inputs": {
        "production-events": {
          "label": "Original production event export",
          "path": "./inputs/production-events.ndjson",
          "kind": "source",
          "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_FILE_SHA256",
          "name": "production-events.ndjson",
          "sourceReference": "Original production OpenLineage export"
        },
        "quality-result": {
          "label": "Complete quality query result",
          "path": "./inputs/quality-result.csv",
          "kind": "result",
          "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_FILE_SHA256",
          "name": "quality-result.csv",
          "mediaType": "text/csv",
          "sourceReference": "Original quality query and run reference"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
~~~

Add tokenFile to the workspace entry when required. Select the operator token for this merchant connection; a separate producer token applies only to native event intake. Its contents remain in the host; tool responses expose workspace identity and input metadata. A configuration supports 1–32 distinct workspace aliases and up to 128 complete input aliases per workspace.

The default host input capacity is 40 MiB. maxInputBytes may raise the host's file-reading capacity to 1 GiB, while the selected native route and original source ceiling still apply. The default native action request is 64 MiB including JSON/base64 overhead; source imports have a 256 MiB wire/decoded ceiling. Configure the receiving host and choose the matching capacity before transferring a larger complete source. A file beyond the configured capacity returns its original size error.

The selected application uses a literal HTTP loopback origin, 127.0.0.1 or ::1. Tool callers choose configured aliases, native entity keys, record collections, and retained object IDs.

## Core client without the full merchant distribution

The call/summary/close owner and host client use Node builtins plus this workspace's native client and pure tool catalog. They can be exercised beside the existing source application:

~~~javascript
import { readLineageWorkspaceConfiguration } from "./mcp-client.mjs";
import { MerchantOpenLineageWorkspaces } from "./mcp.mjs";
const host = await readLineageWorkspaceConfiguration("/absolute/path/to/openlineage-host.json");
const owner = new MerchantOpenLineageWorkspaces({ openlineageWorkspaces: host });
try {
  const selected = await owner.call("merchant_lineage_workspaces", {});
  const metadata = await owner.call("merchant_lineage_workspace_metadata", { workspace: "operations" });
  console.log(selected, metadata);
} finally {
  await owner.close();
}
~~~

Closing the borrowed owner aborts its local waits and drains its tasks. The native server remains available to its browser and other clients.

## Operator workflow

1. Call merchant_lineage_workspaces to choose the original workspace and inspect complete input aliases.
2. Call merchant_lineage_workspace_metadata and retain revision. Page merchant_lineage_records_read with collection, expectedRevision, offset, and limit. Follow nextOffset until null.
3. Verify an input with merchant_lineage_input. Import a complete source with merchant_lineage_import_file, supplying input, expectedSha256, operationId, and expectedRevision. Native merchant_lineage_source_import also accepts complete text or base64 within the host's tool request capacity.
For a compressed source, keep the original .gz input alias and its wire SHA-256, and pass contentEncoding: "gzip" to merchant_lineage_import_file or merchant_lineage_source_import. The saved request retains this encoding alongside the original bytes and operation identity. merchant_lineage_source_read with decode: true returns the original base64 plus verified decodedBase64 and decodedSha256; object ranges and source downloads remain the original compressed bytes. [PRODUCERS.md](PRODUCERS.md) also connects native producer HTTP clients to this same workspace.

4. Inspect original entities with merchant_lineage_entity_read. Read their complete events, facets, source attribution, and reviews. Use merchant_lineage_lineage_read for upstream/downstream nodes and edges at a chosen depth.
5. Save a named edition with merchant_lineage_edition_save. Compare it with another edition or the current workspace using merchant_lineage_edition_compare.
6. Save named review decisions with merchant_lineage_review_save, including title, reason, entityKeys, decision, and the optional editionId.
7. Attach a complete result with merchant_lineage_attach_file. Include its host-pinned input and SHA-256, entityKeys, editionId, sourceReference, operationId, and expectedRevision. Query or experiment details may accompany the attachment.
8. Call merchant_lineage_workspace_export with includeApplication true. Read all bytes of that retained export with merchant_lineage_export_read and its returned ID.
9. Receive and reopen the complete package through the original CLI:

~~~sh
node cli.mjs receive --input openlineage-workspace.json --out /absolute/path/to/received-project
node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/path/to/received-project --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

The complete source export includes the original application and the retained event, source, edition, review, and result records.

## Complete records and original bytes

| Operation | Continuation |
| --- | --- |
| merchant_lineage_records_read | Keep collection, edition, and expectedRevision; continue at nextOffset until null. |
| merchant_lineage_object_read | Keep original id; concatenate each decoded base64 range in offset order until complete. |
| merchant_lineage_export_read | Keep export id; concatenate ranges in offset order until complete. |
| merchant_lineage_source_read | Returns the complete original object as base64 when it fits the tool response. |
| merchant_lineage_report_read | Returns complete JSON, CSV, or HTML report text. |

Range reads default to 262,144 bytes and accept 1–4,194,304 bytes. Verify the final reconstructed file's SHA-256 against its original id. Range bytes, offset, nextOffset, totalBytes, and completion state remain explicit.

Tool requests accept 128 KiB; host file aliases carry larger complete inputs. Complete responses accept 8 MiB. When an entity/report/record page exceeds that response capacity, use smaller native record pages or original object/export ranges. Oversized read responses return an explicit size error. A successfully saved mutation with an oversized response returns outcome CONFIRMED, its original operation ID and revision, and a complete export retrieval route. Its responseView.complete is false; the full saved response remains in the original operation journal and complete workspace package.

## Recovery and concurrency

Every mutation requires an operationId and expectedRevision. The native workspace stores successful operations with their input identity and replays a completed operation before checking its old revision.

After timeout, cancellation, connection interruption, or an unexpected server error, repeat the identical operation, including its original ID, expected revision, file SHA, and full input. The borrowed client's metadata records active operations and uncertain operation identities. The original workspace's operations collection is the durable server record; retaining the caller's exact request supports recovery across client restarts.

The client pins the workspace and application instance at attachment. A later server restart leaves that pin in place. Call merchant_lineage_connection to inspect the current host-selected instance, then merchant_lineage_reconnect with its exact expectedInstanceId. This explicitly connects to the same configured workspace. Recover the original mutation afterwards.

A revision conflict includes currentRevision. Read the changed workspace, review the intended edit against it, and submit the reviewed edit with a new operationId and current expectedRevision.

merchant_lineage_cancel cancels one active local wait by operationId. Its response identifies cancellation requested; the native server may already have saved that operation, so recover the original request.

## Errors and effects

Authentication, startup identity changes, source SHA changes, validation, revision conflicts, active writer responses, connection interruption, and uncertain mutations remain distinct. Provider errors carry their native HTTP status and details. Mutation recovery details include operation ID, expected revision, payload hash, configured workspace, and attached instance.

Read tools use the configured local workspace. Imports, saved editions, reviews, result attachments, and exports use the original native actions. Workspace exports write their retained complete package in the original project.

# Receive original pipeline events

Use the workspace's existing `POST /api/v1/lineage` endpoint for native OpenLineage HTTP producers. The same workspace receives the source, projects lineage, saves reviewed editions, and exports the complete application and original files.

The receiver accepts a JSON event, JSON event array, or JSON lines, either uncompressed or with `Content-Encoding: gzip`. It keeps the actual request body. For gzip, the source ID is the SHA-256 of the compressed wire bytes; the source record also retains the decoded byte count and SHA-256. Complete original downloads return those compressed bytes. Source inspection can display the verified decoded JSON.

## Start the selected workspace

Use the installed `starforge openlineage` command, or the received application's `node /absolute/application/cli.mjs` entry. The following examples use the native entry directly.

For an authenticated producer, select two different private token files. The operator token accesses the whole workspace. The producer token admits original events only at the native producer endpoint.

```sh
node /absolute/application/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /absolute/lineage-project \
  --port 8767 \
  --token-file /absolute/private/operator-token \
  --producer-token-file /absolute/private/producer-token
```

Both tokens must contain at least 24 characters, and they must differ. Keep the token files with the selected host's existing secret configuration. The application writes its nonsecret current connection to `/absolute/lineage-project/connection.json`.

The default listener is `127.0.0.1`. A pipeline running on that same host can use it directly. A remote deployment needs the operator's existing authenticated transport to this listener, retaining its expected Host and origin. The workspace does not deploy a proxy or alter network configuration.

A local unprotected workspace can omit both token flags. A workspace configured with only the operator token retains its existing common-token behavior.

## Generate private producer settings

Generate settings from the actual connection file, using the producer's token file:

```sh
node /absolute/application/cli.mjs producer-config \
  --connection /absolute/lineage-project/connection.json \
  --token-file /absolute/private/producer-token \
  --client python \
  --compression gzip \
  --timeout 30 \
  --out /absolute/private/python-openlineage.yaml
```

The command creates a new private file and prints its path, workspace identity and authentication status. It keeps the token out of standard output. The output is a complete JSON document, also valid YAML, containing the client's native `transport` configuration. Point the producer's existing OpenLineage configuration loader at that file using `OPENLINEAGE_CONFIG`.

For the Java client, select `--client java`. The Python configuration uses `timeout` in seconds and `custom_headers`; the Java configuration uses `timeoutInMillis` and `headers`. Both select HTTP, the original lineage endpoint, gzip, bearer API-key authentication, and `X-OpenLineage-Workspace` with the original workspace ID. That header survives a server restart and rejects an accidentally substituted workspace.

Use `--compression identity` for an uncompressed client. Produce a new settings file from the observed connection when the host address or port changes. The server instance ID belongs to operator reconnect handling; it is deliberately absent from a producer configuration that continues across ordinary restarts.

The browser's **Producer intake** control shows this same endpoint, original workspace identity, active queue and server counters. It can create the same complete client settings after the operator enters the selected producer token locally. A downloaded settings file contains that selected token and belongs in the producer's private configuration.

## Acknowledgement, retries and simultaneous arrivals

The receiver acknowledges an event only after the original source, event references and operation result have been committed through the workspace's atomic writer. Concurrent producer bodies wait in that server's append queue. An unacknowledged body stays the producer's responsibility if the process or connection is lost.

The default operation ID is `intake-` followed by the SHA-256 of the unchanged wire body. A client can instead supply its stable original `Idempotency-Key`. Retrying the same bytes, source name, reference and encoding returns the original committed response with `replayed: true`. It does not advance the workspace revision again. A changed request under the same explicit operation ID returns a conflict.

Native appends select the current revision inside the original writer. They do not overwrite earlier events or reviewed editions. If a sender explicitly supplies `If-Match`, that sender's revision must still match. Browser and SDK review, edition, attachment and explicit source-import operations continue using their existing revision checks.

| Response | Meaning and continuation |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Original source and operation are committed, or this is their exact saved replay. The response includes source identity, byte metadata, counts and original revision. |
| `400` / `415` | Correct the invalid JSON, gzip, request header or unsupported media/encoding before sending that corrected request. |
| `401` / `403` | Use the selected token, host and origin. Producer credentials apply only to the native intake endpoint. |
| `409` | The workspace pin, explicit revision or existing operation identity differs. Inspect the original selection and request. |
| `413` | The wire or decoded source exceeds its configured capacity. Select an appropriate source or explicitly configure that receiving host. |
| `503` with `Retry-After: 1` | The queue or original writer is occupied. Retry the same original body. |
| `500` / interrupted response | Preserve the original body and operation ID. A retry reconciles any commit that completed before the response was lost. |

An equivalent JSON event encoded differently has a different original source identity. Canonical event identity still joins duplicate event observations, retaining every contributing source location. Recompression may therefore create another original compressed source while retaining the same logical event.

## Capacity and observation

Default producer capacity is 64 admitted requests, 128 MiB of retained wire bodies, 64 MiB per wire body, and 64 MiB of decoded content per body. Decoding happens within the serialized commit path. The SDK host's `startServer({ producerLimits })` can select explicit limits. The decoded/source ceiling is 256 MiB; the wire buffer must accommodate one maximum-size body.

A body that cannot be admitted receives retryable backpressure. The response does not claim that its source was saved. The configured byte limits cover retained wire bodies and each decoded body; parsing and immutable workspace projection also require memory.

`GET /api/producer` reports admitted, committed, replayed, rejected and failed requests, accepted wire bytes, current queue occupancy, and the last committed source and operation. These are counters for the current server instance. Complete saved sources and operation history remain in the original workspace across restarts. Use the existing `records.read` operation with the current revision and continue every returned page for durable history.

## Native client and merchant operation

The supplied `LineageClient` can send the same native producer request:

```js
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { LineageClient } from "./client.mjs";

const producer = new LineageClient(originalConnection.url, {
  token: selectedProducerToken,
  expectedWorkspaceId: originalConnection.workspaceId
});
const originalWire = await readFile("/absolute/source/events.json.gz");
const saved = await producer.emitSource(originalWire, {
  name: "events.json.gz",
  contentEncoding: "gzip"
});
```

Keep `originalWire`, its source metadata and any explicit operation ID unchanged for response-loss recovery. The client performs one original HTTP call and returns the server's saved acknowledgement.

An operator can import a compressed original through `source.import` with its complete base64 body and `contentEncoding: 'gzip'`. The original Merchant Workspace source-import tool and host-selected import-file tool accept the same encoding. They retain their explicit operation/revision and pinned input-SHA contracts.

`source.read({ id, decode: true })` returns the original base64 body and, for gzip, the verified decoded base64 body and decoded hash. The normal object/range download still returns the exact original wire file. Complete paging and export receiving remain the existing merchant operations.

## Original client contract

The receiving behavior follows the original [Python HTTP transport configuration](https://openlineage.io/docs/client/python/configuration/) and [Java HTTP transport configuration](https://openlineage.io/docs/client/java/configuration/), checked on 2026-10-12. The pinned Python transport used for the implementation review is [http.py at 07864a6b](https://github.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/blob/07864a6b5f5d30b878e157eba8409dda84d68d4f/client/python/src/openlineage/client/transport/http.py), Git blob `c23dfdfcad2d2b3800d887723e34c5eb1d482d05`. It emits JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`, optional gzip and bearer API-key authentication, and supports the configured custom headers. Upstream event bodies and their original license remain in this application's existing fixture inventory.

# OpenLineage operations — installed product

The `openlineage-operations` selection delivers the complete lineage workspace through the existing Starforge builder, installer, Applications lifecycle and merchant host. Operators can receive original producer events, inspect jobs, runs and datasets, review a saved edition, attach its complete result files, and hand an editable workspace to another operator.

## Product entry points

| Surface | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| Browser | **OpenLineage operations** in the existing Applications view |
| Operator CLI | `starforge openlineage` |
| Native API and typed client | The original HTTP server and `./seller/openlineage` package export |
| Direct MCP | `starforge openlineage mcp --workspace DIR` |
| Managed merchant agent | The source-owned OpenLineage workspace provider |
| Source-selected installation | `--selection openlineage-operations` |
| Complete customer handover | Original events, results, editions, reviews, operation history and portable application |

The [complete source/API guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/README.md) explains producer intake, entity and facet semantics, the API catalog, typed client, and direct receiving. The [source contract](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/SOURCE_CONTRACT.md) identifies the original upstream contracts and untouched examples.

## Build the selected source

Choose `openlineage-operations` in the existing Runtime workspace's **Build a product** view. Select the full source commit, review the product, and build into a new owned output directory. The resulting archive opens in the existing **Source & profile** view.

The same operation is available from the source checkout:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-workspace-checkout \
  --ref ORIGINAL_FULL_COMMIT \
  --selection openlineage-operations \
  --out /absolute/openlineage-release
```

The returned archive, SHA-256 and source manifest identify this exact product edition. The manifest retains the original selection, contributions, source paths, original Git objects and complete byte identities. Use that returned archive when installing or transferring the product.

Continue an interrupted build through its original output:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-workspace-checkout \
  --out /absolute/openlineage-release --resume
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --out /absolute/openlineage-release --status
```

The saved output retains its original commit and selection. A different product or source edition uses a different output. The [maintained source-build guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-workspace/SOURCE_BUILDS.md) covers browser operation, offline Git acquisition, original locks and continuation.

## Install the maintained merchant profile

The portable OpenLineage application itself uses Node builtins and runs on Node 22 or later. The maintained merchant installation uses the existing Node 22.16+ runtime and its selected native, schema, OpenAPI, MCP and operator dependencies. Their exact versions come from the selected source and retained dependency lock.

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs prepare \
  --dir /absolute/openlineage-runtime \
  --archive /absolute/openlineage-release/ORIGINAL_PACKAGE.tgz \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp --operator

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs install \
  --dir /absolute/openlineage-runtime

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs inspect \
  --dir /absolute/openlineage-runtime --load --source

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs run \
  --dir /absolute/openlineage-runtime -- openlineage --help
```

Use the original installer's dependency adoption and offline transfer flows when an existing complete dependency tree is available. Its retained lock, source inspection and READY state stay with the same runtime. The [runtime installation guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/RUNTIME_INSTALL.md) provides these operations.

The commands below use the installed `starforge` executable. If it is not on PATH, use the same `runtime-install-cli.mjs run --dir /absolute/openlineage-runtime --` prefix and pass the command shown after `starforge`.

```sh
starforge source
starforge registrations --source openlineage-workspace
starforge merchant-providers list
```

## Open the customer's workspace

Initialize a new private project once:

```sh
starforge openlineage init \
  --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
  --title "Pipeline operations"

starforge openlineage serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/lineage --port 0
```

Open the printed URL. For managed operation, register the READY runtime in the existing Runtime workspace, open **Applications**, and select **OpenLineage operations**. Choose this initialized workspace and an optional private token file. Review and save the launch, then use the existing Start, Open and Stop controls. Reopen a received project through the same application entry.

The application verifies its workspace identity and server instance when connecting. The browser retains an exact pending mutation before sending it. If a response is interrupted, reopen the same workspace and recover that original action. A revision conflict presents the current state for review before a new intended change.

## Receive producer originals and save a review

Import the complete producer JSON, event array or NDJSON file:

```sh
starforge openlineage import \
  --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
  --input /absolute/producer/events.ndjson \
  --name events.ndjson \
  --source https://YOUR_PRODUCER/retained-run-log \
  --operation-id original-producer-capture

starforge openlineage edition \
  --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
  --title "Reviewed production run" \
  --operation-id original-reviewed-edition
```

The source reference is retained metadata. Imports preserve every original byte, the producer's namespaced identities, original event content and its source positions. Later observations retain their original content while the operational view applies the relevant facet replacement and deletion rules.

Use the browser's entity inspector to follow the original event and active lineage. Save a reasoned review against the chosen edition and entities. Attach an existing result file with its source reference and original query where applicable. The result's complete bytes remain attached to that edition even after later imports.

Compare saved editions before adopting an upstream change. The full report and source downloads preserve the inspection context. The [source contract](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/SOURCE_CONTRACT.md) describes how explicit lineage, input/output boundaries, supported schema versions and historical observations are represented.

## Connect native pipeline producers

The existing producer endpoint accepts original JSON/NDJSON or gzip bodies.
Open **Producer intake** in the browser to inspect the current endpoint, queue
and server counters and download complete Python or Java settings. The
`producer-config` CLI generates the same private settings from the current
connection file. Keep the original workspace pin across ordinary server restarts.

For a dedicated producer credential, start the same workspace with a private
operator token and a different producer token:

```sh
starforge openlineage serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/lineage --port 8767 \
  --token-file /absolute/private/operator-token \
  --producer-token-file /absolute/private/producer-token

starforge openlineage producer-config \
  --connection /absolute/private/lineage/connection.json \
  --token-file /absolute/private/producer-token \
  --client python --compression gzip \
  --out /absolute/private/openlineage.yaml
```

Both token values contain at least 24 characters. Point the existing producer's
`OPENLINEAGE_CONFIG` at the complete generated file. The browser and managed
merchant use the operator credential; the producer credential admits event
bodies at `POST /api/v1/lineage`.

A successful producer response follows the original atomic source commit.
Concurrent bodies use its serial append queue. Retry an unacknowledged unchanged
body and operation identity after retryable backpressure. Original wire and
decoded identities, client-specific setup, capacity and complete continuation
are documented in the [producer guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/PRODUCERS.md).

## Native agents share the same owner

The direct CLI, browser, typed client and MCP interfaces call the same revisioned workspace. Managed merchant access connects to the running application's original connection file and binds the selected workspace and instance. File-input aliases can name complete original event or result files with their SHA-256, so the operator can transfer actual retained files through the existing private configuration.

Use the [merchant operating guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/openlineage-workspace/MERCHANT.md) for provider setup, tools, exact request recovery and complete downloads. `workspace.metadata` returns the current revision and retained counts. `records.read` pages through complete collections at that same revision; continue `nextOffset` until it is null. The `operations` collection is the complete workspace journal and is read without an edition restriction. It retains original saved outcomes for recovery.

Preserve the same operation ID and original mutation arguments after an uncertain response. Reconnecting to a restarted application is explicit. A new intended action receives a new ID after its current state has been reviewed.

## Complete delivery and receiving

Create the full editable workspace package:

```sh
starforge openlineage export \
  --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
  --out /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json

starforge openlineage report \
  --workspace /absolute/private/lineage \
  --format html --out /absolute/delivery/openlineage-report.html
```

The workspace package includes all retained source and result objects, saved state, editions, review history, original operation outcomes, and every portable application file. Each original object and application file has a byte length and SHA-256. Receiving derives event attribution and edition membership from the original source bytes.

Receive into a new directory and reopen the original workspace identity:

```sh
starforge openlineage verify \
  --input /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json

starforge openlineage receive \
  --input /absolute/delivery/openlineage-workspace.json \
  --out /absolute/received-lineage

node /absolute/received-lineage/application/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /absolute/received-lineage --port 0
```

The receiving directory contains the original state and objects plus its own editable `application/` source. The receiver can inspect, import, review, attach results, export and reopen this same project. The maintained installed application can also select that received workspace.

For large exported packages, the typed client and merchant adapter support complete range downloads with original byte identities. Keep the same original export ID, destination and partial download record when continuing. A completed identical destination is reused.

Deliver the selected source archive and its installer receipt alongside the customer's workspace package when the recipient needs the entire managed merchant installation. Follow the original Runtime transfer workflow to carry its selected dependency profile and complete installation. Keep project data in its private project directory across runtime upgrades.

## Run the complete native operating journey

The source includes `RECEIVING.mjs`, a complete original operation using the retained upstream OpenLineage examples and actual native HTTP, client and MCP. It imports complete sources, saves and compares editions, inspects lineage, reviews an entity, attaches an original reference file, recovers an original mutation, writes complete reports, downloads the full export, receives into an independent directory and starts that received application.

From the OpenLineage source directory:

```sh
node RECEIVING.mjs /absolute/new-openlineage-receiving
```

Use a new owned receiving directory for a new run. The programme records its actual progress and final result in that directory, preserves its complete generated outputs, and closes its two native servers. Browser operation can be reviewed by opening the received workspace through the normal serve command.

The companion producer operation exercises native gzip and simultaneous HTTP
arrivals, original replay, explicit writer backpressure, server restart and
independent receiving of all compressed originals:

```sh
node PRODUCER_RECEIVING.mjs /absolute/new-openlineage-producer-receiving
```

Its saved operation file retains the original workspace and stage identities.
An interrupted stage continues through the same directory. The complete
producer guide explains the generated files and continuation.
